---
title: "Additional Citation Options"
---

This tutorial starts with ordinary native citations, then changes one marked
citation. The repository's `README.md` contains the installation and advanced syntax,
style/processor, customisation and compatibility reference.

## 1. Render the page

From this checkout, run `quarto render example.qmd --to html` or use the editor's
Render control. `_quarto.yml` already selects the local filter, bibliography and
`citeproc: false`. In a separate project, install the extension, copy this file
and `references.bib`, then apply the README's activation YAML. A GitHub
installation uses the owner-qualified selector.

## 2. Compare two presentations

Ordinary narrative citation: @bergelson_1996.

The same facts without round delimiters: [@bergelson_1996]{.no-paren}.

The QMD for the second is `[@bergelson_1996]{.no-paren}`. Remove `.no-paren`,
render again and check that normal punctuation returns. Both versions retain
the citation key and bibliography entry. No browser script is involved.

## 3. Add native citation features

Native citation syntax remains available:

- Narrative: @bergelson_1996
- Parenthetical: [@bergelson_1996]
- Suppress author: [-@bergelson_1996]
- Locator: [@bergelson_1996, sec. 1]

## 4. Explore the extra presentation options

- Remove the round delimiters: [@bergelson_1996]{.no-paren}
- Remove the outer round delimiters of a parenthetical citation:
  [[@bergelson_1996]]{.no-paren}
- Remove the parenthesised segment of a narrative citation:
  [@bergelson_1996]{.remove-paren}
- Keep surrounding text and formatting:
  [See **@bergelson_1996** for the discussion]{.no-paren}.

These classes edit punctuation. They do not select CSL author/year fields.
Applying `.remove-paren` to an entirely parenthetical citation removes all
of its visible text; the bibliography entry remains.

## 5. Optionally use a different admitted style

The default example needs no downloaded CSL. For the exact separately downloaded
APA file linked in the README, add ordinary `csl: apa.csl` and `lang: en-GB`
(or the finite `en-US` / `fr-FR` cases). Keep the filter and
`citeproc: false`. Changed styles and unadmitted locales retain native
citations; no CSL or locale is inferred from its filename.

## 6. Optionally apply the operation in an abstract

After the body example works, add an abstract and this explicit setting to
document/project YAML, replacing the reference with one from your bibliography:

```yaml
additional-citation-options:
  metadata: [abstract]
abstract: |
  A summary with [@bergelson_1996]{.no-paren}.
```

Render and inspect the summary. Remove the `metadata` option and rerender to
restore native abstract punctuation; the body examples stay active. This also
works when the body has no marked citation. Title/social/description metadata
retain normal native output. Unknown styles and alternate processors keep the
README's fallback. These controls do not approve citation facts or style quality.

## Citation in a definition heading

::: {#def-example}
## [[@bergelson_1996, sec. 1]]{.no-paren}

This is an authoring demonstration, not a mathematical definition.
:::

## Next steps

Use IDs from your own bibliography. Open `README.md` in the repository and consult
its syntax reference for marked spans and supported scope before changing the
CSL or processor. The exact current Manchester CSL is now admitted alongside
the historical version and the default style. To try it, download the CSL file
separately and use the README's ordinary `csl:` setting; no additional adapter
switch is needed. Changed or customised styles keep their normal citations and
skip these extra punctuation operations until separately verified.
